Article Title: ‘Term UN experts is oxymoron’: Rubio calls anti-EC protests ‘domestic political matter’
Article Text:
Marco Rubio says Washington will not comment on India's handling of anti-EC protests, leaving the matter to Indians to decide

India rejects UN experts' allegations

NEW DELHI: US secretary of state Marco Rubio on Wednesday dismissed the term “UN experts” as an “oxymoron” when asked about the United Nations' criticism of India's handling of anti-Election Commission protests, calling the issue a "domestic political matter" that should be decided by Indians.Asked about protests by opposition parties and students in India and UN experts' allegations of a crackdown on demonstrators, Rubio said Washington would not interfere in the country's internal politics."Well the UN experts, my favourite. The UN experts is an oxymororn," he said.He added that India was a democracy with elections and said he would not comment on its domestic political matters.“No, it's a domestic political matter. This is a democracy, they have elections here. I am not going to opine on their political matters,” Rubio said.Rubio distinguished peaceful demonstrations from riots involving vandalism and destruction of property, saying the ability to express differing political opinions was an important feature of democratic societies."I am not talking about the riots, what you see in Europe. They are vandalizing and breaking and burning down buildings. I am not talking about that," he said.Rubio's remarks come amid a diplomatic exchange over concerns raised by UN experts about India's handling of protests. The experts had alleged restrictions on peaceful assembly and raised concerns over the alleged excessive use of force against demonstrators and reports of enforced disappearances.India pushed back against the criticism at the United Nations on Tuesday, rejecting what it described as attempts to portray the country negatively on the basis of unverified allegations and incomplete statistics.Indian diplomat Barkha Tamrakar told the UN that constitutional safeguards, including Article 21, protect human rights and ensure due process.“India firmly opposes any attempt to convert unverified allegations, incomplete statistics, or a report that contains no India country observation into a negative characterization of the world's largest democracy,” Tamrakar said.“Human rights should not be used as an instrument of political pressure or selective country targeting,” she added.India also called for impartial and evidence-based engagement on human rights, arguing against what it described as selective scrutiny of countries.
Article Summary: US secretary of state Marco Rubio says Washington will not comment on India's handling of anti-Election Commission protests. Rubio calls UN experts' allegations of a crackdown on demonstrators an "oxymoron" He says the issue is a "domestic political matter" that should be decided by Indians.

Article Title: ‘Get your facts straight’: BJP accuses Rahul Gandhi of hypocrisy over RSS remarks on women’s rights
Article Text:
BJP hits back at Rahul Gandhi over RSS remarks on gender inequality

BJP questions Rahul Gandhi's understanding of RSS

Telangana BJP chief targets Congress over women's reservation

What Rahul Gandhi said about RSS

NEW DELHI: Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) on Wednesday hit back at Congress leader Rahul Gandhi over his remarks accusing the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) of gender inequality, with party leaders alleging hypocrisy and questioning his understanding of the organisation.BJP national spokesperson CR Kesavan accused the Raebareli MP of hypocrisy over his comments on respecting women, while party MLA Ram Kadam said the Congress leader should study the RSS before making allegations against it.Kesavan alleged that the Congress leader's remarks about treating women with respect were contradicted by his conduct towards a woman police personnel and a woman journalist."Rahul Gandhi sermonising about treating women with respect is indeed most sadistic and cruel given how Rahul Gandhi in the recent past has misbehaved improperly and inappropriately with both a female police personnel and a woman journalist," Kesavan said.He also questioned Rahul’s response to allegations against a Congress MP facing multiple charges of sexually harassing students."Rahul Gandhi's farcical remarks are highly hypocritical because if Rahul Gandhi truly even had an iota of respect for our women's power, Rahul Gandhi would have squarely condemned and taken action against the Congress MP who is now facing multiple charges of sexually harassing students," Kesavan said.The BJP spokesperson further accused the Congress of failing to advance women's empowerment during its years in power, claiming that the party had not passed the women's reservation Bill despite governing the country for more than 55 years at the Centre."Right from Nehru's Congress to Rahul Gandhi's Congress, the Congress party has always been against women empowerment which is why despite being in power for more than 55 years at the Centre, the Congress party never bothered to pass the women's reservation bill," he said.BJP MLA Ram Kadam also criticised Rahul's remarks, arguing that the Congress leader should verify his claims before making public statements about the RSS."Rahul Gandhi frequently makes remarks about the RSS. While he certainly has the right to engage in political accusations, counter-accusations, and sharp criticism, he should do so only after proper study," Kadam said.Questioning the former Congress president's claim about the organisation's treatment of women, Kadam said the RSS had a women's wing that operated across the country."Is he unaware that the RSS also has a wing for women? It operates across the entire country, and women work within it with the same level of prominence as men," he said.Kadam also questioned whether Rahul was making statements on social media without sufficient information."Are you going to tweet from your X handle based on incomplete information just to grab headlines? At the very least, get your facts straight. Tweeting with such a childish, immature mindset does not befit a leader of the opposition," he said.Telangana BJP state president N Ramchander Rao also accused Rahul of overlooking what he described as the male-dominated nature of the Congress. He challenged the party to explain its record on women's representation and support for the 33 per cent women's reservation proposal."Rahul Gandhi seems to be forgetting how male-dominated his party is. Wherever they are ruling, let him answer how many women chief ministers there are. This BJP has got a woman chief minister in the capital," Rao said.Questioning the Congress's position on women's reservation, he said, "If you are not anti-woman, then why don't you support 33% women reservation with delimitation? Your party failed to pass that legislation in the Parliament several times."Rao also challenged Rahul's claim that women supported his political fight against the RSS, arguing that the Congress's actions did not match its stated position on women's empowerment."Rahul Gandhi has claimed that women are with him, and 'smash patriarchy' is only a slogan for him. But in practice, Congress is against women," he said.Rao also raised the issue of a Congress MP who, he alleged, had been suspended and removed from service at Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU) over a sexual harassment case."What action have you taken against your own MP who has been suspended and removed from service in JNU over a sexual harassment case?... This is a hypocritical stance of the Congress party," he said.The BJP leaders were responding to a Rahul's post on X on Tuesday, in which the leader of the opposition in the Lok Sabha described the RSS as an "all-male, anti-constitutional cult" and alleged that it believed women were the property of men."The RSS is an all-male, anti-constitutional cult that believes women are the property of men. I believe in Shiva-Shakti. That's why it gives me such joy to fight them. What's beautiful is that many of their 'own' women are on my side," Rahul wrote.His remarks were the latest in a series of attacks on the RSS. On October 10, the Raebareli MP had accused the Delhi Police of encouraging violence by RSS-BJP supporters against women protesters and young people amid political tensions over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.Rahul has also criticised RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat, accusing him, Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Union home minister Amit Shah and others of being on the opposing side of his political fight.Separately, the Vishwa Hindu Parishad (VHP) also criticised Rahul's comments. VHP national spokesperson Vinod Bansal accused the Congress leader of "mental bankruptcy" and alleged that he was using religion for political purposes."... Leaders like Rahul Gandhi suffer from 'Mental Bankruptcy'. He failed to notice women at RSS events. Vijayadashami celebrations were held across the country yesterday, and I personally attended three of them. Families were present at every event. Congress has travelled the world criticising the RSS, and everyone knows what it has gained or lost in the process..."The remarks came as the RSS held its annual Vijayadashami celebrations at Reshimbagh Ground in Nagpur on Tuesday, during the concluding year of its centenary celebrations.
Article Summary: BJP hits back at Rahul Gandhi over his remarks accusing the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh of gender inequality. Party leaders allege hypocrisy and question Rahul's understanding of the organisation. Telangana BJP state president N Ramchander Rao also accused Rahul of overlooking what he described as the male-dominated nature of the Congress.

Article Title: Identify, defeat forces against India: Modi calls for unity, self-reliance
Article Text:
PM Modi said all institutions and political parties must stand together in the national interest (Photo: PTI).

NEW DELHI: Calling for a united fight against forces seeking to divide society, undermine India's dignity and attack its culture, Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Tuesday urged all political parties and national institutions to put the country first. Stressing that national self-respect and faith in one's own strength were essential for progress, he said India must protect its cultural identity while building the capabilities to overcome challenges without depending on others.“We must identify the enemies of Mother India. We must defeat them,” Modi said at the Vijayadashami celebrations in east Delhi. “The forces that hurt the honour and dignity of the country, the people who divide society, the mentality of those who hate our culture — these are the enemies of the country.”Quoting a Vedic verse, Modi said all institutions and political parties must stand together in the national interest. “We must fight the enemies of the country together,” he said, calling for a collective commitment to “Nation First”.His remarks came hours after RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat , speaking in Nagpur, cited political upheavals in France, Albania, Nepal and Bangladesh while warning against attempts to bring about regime change in India.Bhagwat also cautioned against protests becoming political tools and urged both authorities and protesters to remain within constitutional limits.Linking national progress to cultural identity, Modi said, “A nation progresses only when it has a sense of self-respect,” adding that heritage played an important role in building that confidence.He said India's cultural treasures had been looted and taken abroad for centuries, but efforts were now underway to restore them. Over 650 ancient idols had been brought back in the past 12 years, he said, also highlighting UNESCO recognition for Indian heritage sites and Diwali.Drawing lessons from Lord Ram's life, Modi stressed self-reliance. Despite the ocean separating him from Lanka, Ram mobilised collective strength, brought together available resources and achieved what appeared impossible.“We must not sit relying on others. We must recognise our own strength. We must have faith in our own resources,” he said, linking the message to the goals of Atmanirbhar Bharat and Viksit Bharat.Describing Vijayadashami as the victory of truth over falsehood, Modi also recalled Ram embracing Nishad Raj and honouring Shabari as examples of compassion and inclusion.He said Ram Rajya represented governance without discrimination, where everyone received justice and equal opportunities. “The objective of power is not to rule, but public welfare,” he said, urging service to the poor and deprived.
Article Summary: PM Narendra Modi urges all political parties and national institutions to put the country first. He said India must protect its cultural identity while building capabilities to overcome challenges without depending on others. “We must identify the enemies of Mother India. We must defeat them,” he said.

Article Title: Shinde calls INDIA bloc ‘ten-headed Ravana’, accuses Uddhav of ‘vote theft’
Article Text:
'You did not even contest the election. You made a backdoor entry and became chief minister. You stabbed the mandate and grabbed the post. It was a huge dacoity against the people's mandate,' Shinde said.

NEW DELHI: Maharashtra deputy chief minister Eknath Shinde on Tuesday accused Uddhav Thackeray of stealing the people's mandate after the 2019 assembly elections and called the INDIA bloc a “ten-mouthed Ravana” whose effigy should be burnt. Addressing his party's Dussehra rally in Mumbai, Shinde attacked the opposition over its allegations of vote theft, accused it of undermining constitutional institutions and said the government would support farmers facing crop losses due to water scarcity.Without naming Shiv Sena (UBT) chief Uddhav Thackeray, Shinde alleged that the actual “vote theft” took place after the 2019 Maharashtra assembly elections, when the undivided Shiv Sena joined hands with the NCP and Congress to form a government.“You did not even contest the election. You made a backdoor entry and became chief minister. You stabbed the mandate and grabbed the post. It was a huge dacoity against the people's mandate,” he said.Shinde questioned the opposition's allegations of irregularities in electoral rolls, saying it had earlier raised concerns over an increase in voter numbers and was now questioning the deletion of names.“This is double standards and a daily show of new drama. The INDIA bloc is a ten-mouthed Ravana, and we need to burn its effigy,” he said, accusing the opposition of seeking to undermine the Constitution drafted by Dr Babasaheb Ambedkar.He also questioned why the opposition had not alleged vote theft when the INDIA bloc won elections in Telangana, Karnataka and Himachal Pradesh. “When you lose, you call it vote chori and start alleging foul play. The INDIA bloc won elections in Telangana, Karnataka and Himachal Pradesh. Why was there no vote chori then?” he asked.Shinde accused the Congress of looting the country for 70 years and alleged that it was now demanding ballot papers after previously winning elections through booth capturing.He also hit out at opposition leaders for their remarks on regime changes in Bangladesh, Nepal and Sri Lanka, accusing them of encouraging anarchy in India.“This is Hindustan, a new India. This is an India that enters Pakistan,” he said, adding that people would teach a lesson to those he described as anti-national.Questioning the opposition's criticism of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union home minister Amit Shah, Shinde said Modi had made India the world's fourth-largest economy and received the highest civilian awards from 36 countries. He also claimed there was no corruption case against the prime minister.“Why use such foul and low language against our PM?” he asked.Shinde further accused opposition leaders of speaking in Pakistan's favour and alleged that their statements were being used to create headlines there. Referring to Captain Smit Machchhar, who saved a plane during an attack, he said the pilot had acknowledged drawing inspiration from Modi.Shinde claimed that Modi, the US president and the Israeli prime minister had congratulated the pilot, while some opposition leaders had not.“Whatever they say here becomes a headline in Pakistan. This is a huge conspiracy...Why do you speak in favour of Pakistan? This is unfortunate. This is sedition and not any kind of love for India,” he alleged.The deputy chief minister also criticised Congress leader Rahul Gandhi for organising a rally against the Supreme Court, alleging that it amounted to an insult to the judiciary and an attack on a constitutional institution.“On the one hand, they hold the Constitution in their hands, and on the other, their actions amount to an attack on it. They are moving towards dividing the country,” he said.Taking a swipe at the opposition's demand for the election of the chief election commissioner, Shinde sarcastically asked whether it would also seek elections for the chief justice of India and municipal corporation chiefs.He alleged that opposition parties were promoting a “fake narrative” of vote theft through rallies in Mumbai while farmers were struggling with crop losses.Turning to the agrarian crisis, Shinde said Maharashtra was facing drought-like conditions as standing crops dried up due to a weak monsoon. He announced that he had dispatched an initial 100 tonnes of foodgrains to distressed farmers as an advance Diwali gift, with more consignments to follow.“Today, I have dispatched the first tranche of 100 tonnes of foodgrains to farmers as an advance Diwali gift. There will be more such rounds of assistance given to farmers,” he said.Shinde said excessive rainfall had washed away land last year, causing serious losses to crops and cattle. This year, the monsoon had failed to provide adequate relief to farmers, he added.“Unfortunately, this year, the monsoon turned its back on farmers. We reached out to distressed farmers who are shedding tears and offered them consolation. This is not the time to politicise the farmers' plight but to extend support to them,” he said.Describing himself as a farmer's son, Shinde said he understood the hardships faced by cultivators and their families. He also defended his work on the ground, taking an indirect swipe at his critics.“Let me make it very clear that I don't only give 'bhashan' (speeches), but also give ration to farmers,” he said.
Article Summary: Eknath Shinde accused Uddhav Thackeray of stealing the people's mandate after the 2019 assembly elections. He called the INDIA bloc a “ten-mouthed Ravana’ whose effigy should be burnt. The Maharashtra deputy chief minister attacked the opposition over its allegations of vote theft.

Article Title: 'Human rights shouldn't be used for political pressure': India amid UN criticism over handling of protests
Article Text:
A protestor is detained by the police during a youth demonstration demanding the resignation of the country's election chief Gyanesh Kumar, in New Delhi, India

Remarks come amid UN experts’ concerns over protests

UN experts flag mass detentions, alleged ill-treatment

NEW DELHI: India on Wednesday asserted that human rights should not be used as an instrument of political pressure or selective targeting of countries, opposing attempts to turn allegations and incomplete statistics into a “negative characterisation” of the world's largest democracy.While speaking at UNGA Third Committee, deputy secretary in the ministry of external affairs Barkha Tamrakar said, "Human rights not to be used as an instrument of political pressure or selective country targeting.""India engages with international human rights mechanisms, but such engagement must be based on dialogue, consultation, cooperation with non-selectivity and transparency as guiding principle," she added."We call on delegations to cite the report faithfully, not to inflate a humanitarian communication into a verdict."She also opposed any "attempt to convert unverified allegations, incomplete statistics or a report that contains no India country observation into a negative characterisation of the world's largest democracy".Tamrakar's remarks came amid concerns raised by UN human rights experts over recent youth-led protests in New Delhi.On Tuesday, more than 20 UN human rights experts in Geneva expressed alarm over what they described as a “repeatedly heavy-handed police response” to peaceful youth-led demonstrations in the national capital.In a statement shared by UN special procedures, the experts alleged that law enforcement agencies had used force against unarmed students, detained protesters arbitrarily and imposed broad restrictions on public gatherings. They called on Indian authorities to respect the right to peaceful assembly and ensure accountability for alleged abuses.“Despite the non-violent nature of the assemblies, law enforcement has deployed force against unarmed students,” the experts said.The experts said hundreds of thousands of students and their supporters had gathered peacefully across the country to protest government decisions concerning the education system and, more recently, voter-roll deletions.They referred to reports that the deletions affected 130 million individuals, reportedly belonging to Muslim, Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe communities.According to the statement, more than 7,000 young people, journalists, human rights defenders, lawyers and political party members were recently detained in New Delhi and taken to detention centres farther away. Their phones were allegedly seized and protest-related material deleted. Most were released after 24 hours, including protest leaders, the experts said.The statement also cited reports of injuries and ill-treatment among protesters, expressing particular concern over allegations of sexual violence and other forms of gender-based abuse during demonstrations and related detentions.The experts also raised concerns over the reported use of Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) to impose broad restrictions on public gatherings, suspend public transportation and enforce internet shutdowns.They said restrictions on peaceful assembly must be lawful, pursue a legitimate objective and be necessary and proportionate.They urged Indian authorities to immediately stop the excessive use of force, lift blanket restrictions on assemblies and refrain from the misuse of digital surveillance, including biometric monitoring and internet disruptions.The UN experts called for an independent, impartial and thorough investigation into the conduct of law enforcement personnel and affiliated forces, urging authorities to ensure accountability, justice and reparations for victims.
Article Summary: India says human rights should not be used as an instrument of political pressure or selective targeting of countries. Remarks come amid UN experts’ concerns over protests in New Delhi. UN experts flag mass detentions, alleged ill-treatment among protesters.

He backed the youth protests, calling them revolutionaries meanwhile asserting his party’s claim to the saffron identity at the party’s annual Dussehra rally at Shivaji Park in Mumbai.According to PTI, Thackeray said young people had the right to protest against alleged electoral irregularities, particularly those affecting new voters. Article Title: Amit Shah meets families of anti-drug campaigners killed in Punjab; targets AAP on open drug trade
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Home minister Amit Shah on Tuesday met the families of three men who allegedly lost their lives after raising their voices against drug peddlers in Punjab, launching a sharp attack on the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) government over the drug menace in the state.During his visit, Shah met the family of late Bikramjit Singh in Gurdaspur, Gulzar Singh's family in Sangrur and the family of anti-drug activist Parvinder Singh Jhota in Mansa, who was shot dead last week.Shah expressed his condolences to Bikramjit Singh's family."Today, at the residence of the family of late Bikramjit Singh ji, who lost his life for raising his voice against the unchecked drug trade in Punjab under the AAP government, I met them in Gurdaspur and expressed my condolences. May God grant them the strength to bear this sorrow," Shah said, ANI reported.Targeting the Bhagwant Mann-led government over the drug menace, Shah said, "The growing web of drugs in Punjab and the emboldened drug traffickers have raised serious questions about the functioning of the AAP government. In the Bhagwant Mann government, on one hand, Punjab's youth is falling prey to drugs, while on the other hand, those who raise their voices against it are not safe.""We are committed to making Punjab, along with the whole of India, drug-free and securing the future of our youth," he added, as per ANIShah also met the family of Gulzar Singh, who committed suicide after facing alleged intimidation for publicly questioning a Punjab minister about the open sale of synthetic drugs ("chitta”).The visit to Mansa came amid a political row over the murder of Jhota. Hours before Shah's visit, Punjab chief minister Bhagwant Mann announced that the state government had decided to transfer the case to the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI), PTI reported.Jhota, known for raising his voice against the illegal sale of addictive substances at chemist shops, was shot dead inside a medical store in a busy marketplace in Mansa on October 13. According to PTI, store owner Ashwani Kumar allegedly opened fire on Jhota after he questioned him over the sale of addictive drugs to an elderly man.The incident took place while Jhota was hosting a Facebook Live. Kumar was taken into custody from Rajasthan's Salasar, PTI reported.The killing has triggered a political slugfest in Punjab, which is scheduled to hold assembly elections early next year. Shah's visits to Gurdaspur, Sangrur and Mansa brought the drug menace and the safety of those campaigning against it into sharp political focus.
Article Summary: Home minister Amit Shah met the families of three men who allegedly lost their lives after raising their voices against drug peddlers in Punjab. Shah launched a sharp attack on the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) government over the drug menace in the state. NEW DELHI: With Pakistan’s deputy PM Ishaq Dar in the room, defence minister Rajnath Singh on Tuesday delivered a strong message against terrorism at the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) meeting in Tajikistan's Dushanbe.Addressing representatives of SCO member countries, Rajnath said terrorism remained one of the biggest threats to peace and development, warning that its impact extended far beyond the loss of innocent lives.“Terrorism not only causes the loss of innocent lives but also disrupts investment and commerce. It radicalises society and deprives our youth of the opportunities they deserve,” the defence minister said.The defence minister stressed that terrorism could not be justified under any circumstances and called for a united approach against those who enable it.“There should be no double standards in dealing with terrorism, and no place for those who finance, support or provide safe havens to terrorists. The entire ecosystem of terrorism must be firmly and collectively dismantled,” he said.Rajnath's remarks come days after he reiterated India’s firm position on crossborder terrorism, warning on October 15 that any further terrorist acts originating from Pakistan would invite an even stronger response.Speaking at the Times Network Defence Conclave in New Delhi, he said India’s commitment to dialogue, coexistence and peaceful dispute resolution should not be mistaken for weakness.“Operation Sindoor, Balakot Airstrikes and Surgical Strikes weren’t just military operations; they symbolised a decisive shift in the nation’s approach, moving from diplomatic condemnation to proactive action aimed at rooting out terrorism by reaching its very source,” Rajnath said.He also said that since 2014, the ‘shelf life’ of most terrorists had fallen to less than a year, with security forces neutralising them within a year of their taking up arms against India.Emphasising the link between strength and peace, Rajnath said India remained committed to peaceful coexistence while staying prepared to deal with threats to its security.“Our commitment to peace remains steadfast, yet we are fully prepared to confront any challenge. Our goal is to build an India that, while advocating for peace, remains vigilant when it comes to security and is fully capable of safeguarding its sovereignty, integrity, and national interests,” he said.On the sidelines of the SCO meeting, Singh held separate meetings with Tajikistan Prime Minister Qohir Rosulzoda and Iran's First Vice President Mohammad Reza Aref.During his meeting with Rosulzoda, Singh highlighted the longstanding civilisational ties and close people-to-people connections between India and Tajikistan.In a post on X, the defence minister said, "Delighted to meet H.E. Mr Qohir Rosulzoda, Prime Minister of Tajikistan at the commencement of SCO Heads of Government meeting in Dushanbe. Underlined the longstanding civilisational ties and deep people to people links between India and Tajikistan."Rajnath also met Aref and shared details of the interaction on X. "Pleasure to meet H.E. Mr Mohammad Reza Aref, First Vice President of Iran on the sidelines of the SCO Heads of Government meeting in Dushanbe," he wrote.Rajnath is representing India at the SCO Council of Heads of Government meeting in the Tajik capital, where leaders and representatives of member countries have gathered to discuss regional cooperation.Ahead of the meeting, Tajikistan President Emomali Rahmon welcomed Singh and other representatives of SCO member countries at the Palace of the Nation in Dushanbe.According to the ministry of defence, the meeting will focus on strengthening cooperation in culture, connectivity, the economy, innovation, investment and people-to-people ties. Members will also review progress in the organisation's financial and institutional functioning.The ministry highlighted India's contributions across various SCO mechanisms, including initiatives in start-ups, digital public infrastructure and cultural exchanges, saying these offered opportunities to advance practical and mutually beneficial cooperation among member countries.

Article Title: A 52-year-old Oregon farmer started building miniature castles from rocks cleared off his land in 1935, turning a winter hobby into a four-acre garden of stone bridges, churches and landmarks
Article Text:
AI Generated

How Danish immigrant began building Petersen Rock Garden at age 52

The stonework that put Petersen Rock Garden on the map

PC: Petersen Rock Garden

The miniature landmarks attract visitors

New owners took steps to restore the historic garden and museum

A historic attraction enters a new chapter

In central Oregon, a collection of ordinary stones became the raw material for an unusual roadside attraction. Rasmus Petersen, a Danish immigrant who had spent much of his life farming near Redmond, started arranging rocks into miniature buildings during the winter of 1935, according to Petersen Rock Garden, Museum and Peacock Sanctuary. He was 52, and what began as a seasonal pastime gradually spread across the land around his home. Small castles, churches, bridges and other structures took shape from stones gathered in the surrounding region, with ponds and planted areas added to the setting. The result became Petersen Rock Garden, a four-acre site that drew thousands of visitors during its early years and remains a recognised part of the area's history. Over time, the garden evolved into a distinctive blend of folk art, craftsmanship and a family-run attraction rooted in Petersen’s vision.Petersen arrived in Oregon in 1905, settling first in Junction City before claiming an 80-acre homestead near Redmond the following year. The land was acquired under the Desert Land Act, a federal scheme intended to encourage settlement and irrigation in arid parts of the American West.Farming became his livelihood, and by the 1920s he had expanded his agricultural holdings to 256 acres, growing hay and grain and keeping livestock.The Great Depression brought difficult conditions for farmers across the country. Petersen adapted by turning to potatoes, but it was away from the demands of agricultural work that he began developing a different kind of project. Reportedly, in 1935, at the age of 52, he started using the colder months to build small structures from rocks cleared from his land. What he made with them would eventually draw attention well beyond his immediate neighbours.The stones were not simply building material. Petersen incorporated local agate, jasper, obsidian and other varieties into his miniature constructions, selecting pieces for their shapes, colours and textures. Bridges linked sections of the garden, while castles, churches and monuments gave the site the appearance of a small settlement assembled from the geology of the region.The work grew over time. Water features, fountains, mosses and flowers became part of the surroundings, adding living elements to the carefully arranged stonework. Petersen also collected stones from within roughly 85 miles of his home, according to the garden's historical account. That broad geographical reach meant the site reflected the variety of material found across central Oregon rather than relying entirely on rocks from a single field.Visitors began arriving while the garden was still developing. By 1938, the attraction had reportedly welcomed more than 7,000 people. What had started as something to occupy the winter months was becoming a destination in its own right.Petersen Rock Garden eventually covered four acres, with its stone creations arranged among landscaped areas and water. Its appeal lay partly in the contrast between the scale of the structures and the work required to assemble them. Buildings and bridges were made from individual stones, placed together to suggest larger architectural forms in miniature.The site also expanded beyond the garden itself. Historical accounts describe a museum, a diner and a pond with islands among its features. Reportedly, by the early 1950s, annual attendance was said to have reached around 120,000 visitors, placing the garden among the roadside attractions that drew travellers exploring Oregon.One plaque on the property sits beneath a miniature Statue of Liberty. It carries the inscription, “Enjoy yourself. It is later than you think.” The wording offers a small glimpse into the garden's character, although its buildings and collections remain the more substantial record of Petersen's years of work.Petersen devoted himself to the project until his death in 1952. His wife, Nyleta Harris, whom he had married in 1950, continued managing the property until she died in 1987. The garden then passed into the care of her daughter, Adele Hegardt, and her husband, Harry. Following Adele's death, her daughter Susan Caward took on responsibility for the site.The stone structures, planted areas and water features all formed part of a landscape that had developed over decades, rather than a conventional museum collection that could be preserved indoors. In 2010, an Oregon family purchased the site, with preservation efforts organised through a nonprofit established to support the garden, museum and peacock sanctuary. The aim was to protect the attraction and restore features associated with its earlier years. A museum refurbishment followed in 2022 after a grant secured through local business Webfoot Home Improvements.More recent efforts have focused on bringing people back into the work of caring for the garden. Since 2022, Marci Wayman has been associated with new ownership and plans to develop the landmark as a community-stewarded nonprofit. Volunteers have helped with restoration and upkeep, while organisers have sought wider participation in deciding how the property should be preserved and used.The garden's future now depends on more than the stonework Petersen left behind. Its museum, landscape and other features need attention if they are to remain accessible, and community involvement has become part of that process. The original structures still connect the site to the farmer who began building them in 1935, long before the garden became a familiar stop for visitors travelling through central Oregon.
Article Summary: Danish immigrant Rasmus Petersen began building Petersen Rock Garden at age 52 in 1935. Small castles, churches, bridges and other structures took shape from stones gathered in the surrounding region. The four-acre site drew thousands of visitors during its early years and remains a recognised part of the area's history.

Article Title: On return from Paris, Punjab CM Bhagwant Mann 'detained for 3 hours' at Delhi airport, fined Rs 50k
Article Text:
Aam Aadmi Party has alleged that Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann was detained at Delhi airport. (File photo)

Poll Vote & Share your view What do you think is most important when handling disputes between state and central governments? Clear communication between both sides Respect for state government authority Transparent decision-making Following established rules and procedures 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion





CHANDIGARH: Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) has alleged that Punjab CM Bhagwant Mann was detained for three hours at Delhi airport late on Oct 19 and challaned Rs 50,000 on his return from a food trade fair in Paris.AAP state media in charge Baltej Pannu said the incident reflects BJP-led Centre’s deliberate attempt to “humiliate” Mann and “undermine Punjab’s dignity.” Pannu alleged, “When the CM returned from Paris and arrived at Delhi airport, he was deliberately detained. Excuses were made that his luggage was ‘still arriving’ or was ‘still being checked’. These were outright lies. After three hours, when Mann ji was allowed to leave, he was issued a challan of Rs 50,000. ”Pannu alleged, “....After three hours, when Mann ji was allowed to leave and was about to depart after placing his luggage in the vehicle, officials came running after him and said that they were under ‘tremendous pressure from above’. Then, they issued an absurd challan of Rs 50,000. This is a direct attack on Punjab’s identity and dignity.”Pannu did not specify why the fine was imposed but alleged that the entire episode was “carried out under orders from above”.This controversy is a continuation of the AAP govt-vs-Centre tussle over Mann’s France visit. After Centre denied political clearance to Mann for the Paris trip, Punjab govt moved the Punjab and Haryana high court, which set aside the Centre’s decision, observing that it “had not explained what that political angle/viewpoint is”.Pannu said that while approving Mann’s France visit, HC had directed that the Punjab CM be accorded due protocol, but such was the “ill intent” of the Centre that even the Consul General in Paris did not come to meet him.“Has any chief minister ever been detained at an airport for three hours in this manner? Has any CM ever been disrespected by being issued a challan of Rs 50,000? This is happening solely because Bhagwant Singh Mann is a Punjabi, is the chief minister of Punjab, and is working day and night for the betterment of Punjab,” Pannu said.He added that there had been four instances when the Centre denied political clearances to Mann to travel abroad. “The Modi govt fears that if the CM travels abroad, he will bring investment and funds from there and put Punjab on the path of progress.”SAD general secretary Bikram Singh Majithia posted on X: “According to sources, they (Mann and his wife) were questioned for hours over allegedly carrying more luggage or money than permitted. They reportedly failed to provide an explanation. They were eventually allowed to leave, considering Mann’s position as chief minister. However, orders were issued to verify the bags of the entire CMO staff.”The AAP leadership alleged that the incident was linked to BJP-led Centre’s “anti-Punjab” bias. Pannu said, “PM Narendra Modi and his govt leave no opportunity to undermine Punjab and Punjabi identity. Whether it is forcibly keeping farmers at Delhi’s borders for 1.5 years or withholding funds rightfully due to Punjab, the Centre has continuously tried to choke Punjab at every level.”
Article Summary: Aam Aadmi Party has alleged that Punjab CM Bhagwant Mann was detained for three hours at Delhi airport late on Oct 19. AAP state media in charge Baltej Pannu said the incident reflects BJP-led Centre’s deliberate attempt to “humiliate” Mann.

Article Title: CJP's Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka move Delhi HC; cases handed to Crime Branch
Article Text:
Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka have approached the Delhi High Court to challenge their judicial custody.





NEW DELHI: CJP 's Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka Tuesday approached Delhi HC challenging their judicial custody, a day before the special executive magistrate decides whether to extend their custody.The two were detained on Oct 13 after they climbed a gate to enter Jantar Mantar, which has been denotified as a protest site, to protest against SIR. They have since spent 7 days in custody - initial five days, followed by a two-day extension that expires on Wednesday. Meanwhile, police have transferred the Oct 13 cases against them to Crime Branch.Das and Ranka have sought an urgent hearing, but the court is closed for Dussehra. If the executive magistrate releases them Wednesday, their petition will become redundant.However, until late Tuesday, the court’s cause list didn’t have any case listed for hearing this week. However, sources said a call will be taken Wednesday if urgent listing has to be permitted and a vacation bench assembled for the same.In their petition, the two said their two-day remand violated the legal procedure and their ‘Right to Liberty’ under Article 21 of the Constitution.They continue to remain in custody for six days despite submitting the required sureties multiple times, it said.“The mandatory procedure under Section 140 BNSS was not followed for rejecting the surety, showing complete misapplication of the law in the impugned order. That delay and obstruction in the acceptance and verification of sureties frustrates the very purpose of release,” the plea said.The plea further argues that restricting the petitioners’ liberty in the interest of public order requires a “proximate and real nexus with disturbance of public order” and not a remote possibility, pointing out that the issue of protest at a denotified site is, at its highest, a question of regulation, not a threat to public order.
Article Summary: CJP's Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka Tuesday approached Delhi HC challenging their judicial custody. The two were detained on Oct 13 after they climbed a gate to enter Jantar Mantar, which has been denotified as a protest site. They have since spent 7 days in custody - initial five days, followed by a two-day extension.

Article Title: ‘Bismillah, c’est les ténèbres’: What does this viral message from French protests mean
Article Text:
A protester holds a placard reading "Bismillah c'est les tenebres" (Bismillah, it's darkness) during a demonstration by French high school and university students in Nantes as part of a nationwide protest movement

What does ‘ bismillah, c’est les ténèbres ’ mean?

Why are French students protesting?

France’s high school protests have given rise to a string of slogans, but one cryptic phrase has emerged as an unlikely rallying cry. “Bismillah, c’est les ténèbres”, also repeated by climate activist Greta Thunberg, has spread from placards outside blockaded schools to viral videos.The phrase originated in a Snapchat message that students suspect was sent by an undercover police officer.Protesters have turned it into a running joke, using it to mock what they believe was an attempt by police to infiltrate their private protest groups. The slogan has since spread beyond France, appearing at demonstrations in Belgium and Italy.Students say it makes fun of someone attempting, and failing, to sound like a teenager, as per Euro News. However, it is seen as a shorthand for a generational divide, as per The New York Times.“Bismillah” is Arabic for “in the name of God” and is traditionally said before beginning a task. In everyday French slang, it can also mean something like “let’s go”.“C’est les ténèbres” translates as “it’s the darkness”. Young people use the expression as slang for a situation that is grim or catastrophic.Together, the words roughly mean “In the name of God, it’s the darkness”. Students have turned the phrase into a joke about what they see as an attempt by suspected undercover officers to imitate youth slang while trying to gather information about protestsThe phrase came from a screenshot of a Snapchat conversation that began circulating in early October, when students were using the platform to organise school blockades.In the message, a user named “Mamadou” asks to join a group, writing: “Hi, in the name of God, it’s the darkness. When’s the blockade, wallah, bro?"However, neither the French police nor the interior ministry has commented on the screenshots, and the identities of the accounts have not been independently verified.Some social media users claimed to have traced the accounts to locations near police stations, but those claims remain unverified.The movement began in Créteil, south-east of Paris, on September 18 and quickly spread across France.Students have protested against long school days, overcrowded classrooms, deteriorating school buildings and teacher absences. Many argue that these problems disproportionately affect working-class suburbs and minority communities.Around 400 schools were closed by blockades on October 2 alone.The student demonstrations later fed into nationwide cost-of-living protests on October 17, which ended in rioting and looting.
Article Summary: “Bismillah, c’est les ténèbres” has spread from placards outside blockaded schools to viral videos. The phrase originated in a Snapchat message that students suspect was sent by an undercover police officer. The slogan has since spread beyond France, appearing at demonstrations in Belgium and Italy.

Article Title: ‘World’s first’: Ukraine claims heavy-lift drone rescued wounded soldier from frontline
Article Text:
Ukraine leveraged a heavy-lift hexacopter drone to successfully evacuate a wounded soldier from a perilous frontline area (92nd Assault Brigade)

Why this is a big deal

Ukraine has turned a heavy-lift drone into a flying ambulance, lifting a wounded soldier out of a frontline kill zone where mines and Russian drone activity had made a ground evacuation too dangerous.According to Ukraine’s official military news agency ArmyInform, Ukrainian forces have evacuated a wounded soldier from a frontline position using a heavy-lift hexacopter after Russian drone activity Znd mined terrain made a ground evacuation too dangerous.The operation, carried out using a drone supplied by Ukrainian manufacturer Gurzuf Defence, is being described by Kyiv as the world’s first such evacuation and highlights how aerial drones could offer a new way to rescue troops from heavily contested battlefields.According to The War Zone (TWZ), the operation involved personnel from Ukraine’s 92nd, 30th and 14th Mechanised Brigades, the 10th Army Corps and Gurzuf Defence. The wounded infantryman belonged to the 30th Mechanised Brigade, while a UAV operator from the same formation piloted the heavy-lift hexacopter. The soldier remained in contact with the operator throughout the extraction.TWZ reported that the aircraft was supplied free of charge by Ukrainian manufacturer Gurzuf Defence.Military specialists worked with the company to adapt the drone for the mission, with the technical solution designed to keep the aircraft stable and prevent excessive swaying or tipping during flight.The footage shows the soldier securing himself beneath the hexacopter with a harness before being lifted into the air. Unlike a conventional medical evacuation helicopter, the drone carried him suspended beneath its frame, without an enclosed cabin or a protected medical compartment.The military said the soldier was rescued successfully and was undergoing treatment and rehabilitation, with his life no longer in danger.Ukraine has increasingly relied on unmanned ground vehicles to deliver supplies and evacuate casualties from exposed positions. However, mines, mud and cratered terrain can prevent ground robots from reaching wounded troops, while hostile drones and artillery make movement through frontline areas dangerous.An aerial platform offers a potential alternative by bypassing ground obstacles and reaching positions inaccessible to ground vehicles.The operation highlights a potential shift in how wounded soldiers could be evacuated from modern battlefields, where drones, landmines and artillery make conventional rescue missions increasingly dangerous.The approach could also expand the role of heavy-lift drones beyond carrying supplies and equipment. If successfully developed for repeated frontline use, these platforms could provide military commanders with another option for recovering injured troops from positions inaccessible to ground vehicles.However, the method has significant limitations. The footage shows the soldier suspended beneath the aircraft, leaving him exposed during flight. The harness-based approach could also prove difficult for unconscious personnel or those too severely injured to secure themselves. The aircraft’s range, endurance and ability to operate reliably under enemy fire remain unclear.
Article Summary: Ukrainian forces have evacuated a wounded soldier from a frontline position using a heavy-lift hexacopter. The operation was carried out using a drone supplied by Ukrainian manufacturer Gurzuf Defence. Unlike a conventional medical evacuation helicopter, the drone carried him suspended beneath its frame, without an enclosed cabin or a protected medical compartment.

Article Title: Lucknow Police double reward for information on absconding model Shraddha Dubey to Rs 50,000
Article Text:
Police have doubled the reward for information leading to Dubey’s arrest from 25,000 to 50,000.





LUCKNOW: Shraddha Dubey, the prime accused in the death of 28-year-old Shiva Sharma , surfaced publicly for the first time in a brief video interview on Sunday, denying allegations of murder even as she remained untraceable to Lucknow Police, who say they are pursuing multiple leads including a suspected Nepal link.Her appearance came amid speculation that she would surrender at Hazratganj police station, a development that did not materialise. Instead, Dubey spoke to a news agency from an undisclosed location in a video lasting three minutes and 56 seconds, disputing the accusation that she and others were involved in Sharma’s death.Police have doubled the reward for information leading to Dubey’s arrest from ₹25,000 to ₹50,000. Her current location has not been officially confirmed, and investigators have not said whether the interview yielded actionable information about her whereabouts. In a parallel move, Hazratganj SHO Vikram Singh was removed and sent to the reserve police lines.In the interview, Dubey claimed Sharma died by suicide after jumping from the fourth floor of her building. She questioned why CCTV footage from the premises had not been released, arguing that it could clarify the sequence of events.Police have not responded publicly to her remarks about the CCTV recordings, and the footage has not been made public.Earlier, DCP Central Vikrant Vir said police teams were working to trace the accused and were close to locating them, but declined to share operational details, citing the risk of information reaching those being sought. Police sources said Dubey’s suspected location was traced to Mahimnagar in Nepal and that three teams were sent across the border to pursue leads. A 16-member team has also been involved in the search, with investigators suspecting Dubey, her sister Rashmi, and their driver were frequently changing locations to evade arrest.An SUV registered in Dubey’s name was earlier found abandoned near Rupaidiha, close to the India-Nepal border, strengthening suspicions she may have travelled in that direction. Police, however, have not publicly established her movements after the vehicle’s recovery.Sharma died on Oct 9 after falling from the fourth floor of a building near Ballu Adda in Lucknow’s Hazratganj area. His mother, Rachna Sharma, accused Dubey and others of involvement, following which a case was registered under Section 103(1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.Dubey rejected claims made by Sharma’s mother and denied that a diary had revealed incriminating details. She also objected to photographs of her with different people circulating on social media and said her sister had no knowledge of the incident.Dubey said she had known Sharma for about four months and claimed he was under financial stress, with debts of ₹16-17 lakh and creditors calling him. She alleged he took jewellery worth ₹5-6 lakh from her residence about a month before his death and promised in a video to return it. These assertions have not been independently verified.Explaining why she left while Sharma was being taken to hospital, Dubey said she had breathing difficulties and personal reasons, and claimed her driver fled after being assaulted. She appealed for a fair investigation, stating no one should be declared guilty before the probe concludes. Police have not confirmed her location or reported her arrest.
Article Summary: Shraddha Dubey, the prime accused in the death of 28-year-old Shiva Sharma, surfaced publicly for the first time in a brief video interview on Sunday. Her appearance came amid speculation that she would surrender at Hazratganj police station, a development that did not materialise. Her current location has not been officially confirmed, and investigators have not said whether the interview yielded actionable information about her whereabouts.

Article Title: ‘Jaldi le kar jaao, Tiger’: Video shows seat switch as Tiger Shroff takes the wheel after attack
Article Text:
Tiger Shroff switched places with his injured driver to expedite his hospital transfer

Lawrence Bishnoi gang claims responsibility for Tiger Shroff attack





MUMBAI: Bollywood actor Tiger Shroff reportedly took the wheel and rushed his injured driver to hospital after unidentified assailants opened fire at his car in Mumbai’s Juhu area on Sunday evening.A video of the incident shows the actor switching seats with his driver after the firing. A woman can be heard saying, “Jaldi le kar jaao, Tiger”.Blood stains are also visible in the aftermath of the attack.Shroff’s driver, Firdaus, sustained a gunshot wound to his left hand, while the actor escaped without any bullet injuries. The incident took place near Pushpa Narsee Park, where the actor’s vehicle was targeted by motorcycle-borne assailants.Another person, an autorickshaw driver, was also injured in the firing, according to police.The video shows Shroff moving into the driver's seat after his driver was injured in the shooting. The actor reportedly took charge of the vehicle to get the injured driver medical attention.Shroff and Firdaus were taken to Nanavati Hospital in Vile Parle. Doctors said the actor had sustained minor abrasions but no bullet wounds, while the driver suffered a gunshot injury to his left hand.The other injured person, an autorickshaw driver identified as Chauhan, was taken to Cooper Hospital with bullet injuries to his chest.The firing took place around 7 pm on Sunday near Pushpa Narsee Park in Juhu, when Shroff was returning in his car. Seven shots were fired in all.Unidentified assailants allegedly opened fire at the vehicle, injuring the driver and another person nearby.Police have launched an investigation and formed multiple teams to identify and apprehend those involved. CCTV footage from the area is being examined, while forensic teams have begun analysing evidence collected from the spot.Anil Pandit and Harman Sandhu, purportedly associated with the Lawrence Bishnoi gang, claimed responsibility for the firing in a social media post and a voice note.The message also threatened people in the Mumbai film industry who work with actor Salman Khan.The authenticity of the claims and their alleged connection to the shooting had not been independently established, and police were investigating the motive behind the attack.Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis spoke to Mumbai Police Commissioner Deven Bharti and directed the police to expedite the investigation and take strict action against those responsible. Fadnavis also spoke to Shroff and assured him, “We are all with you. We will trace and apprehend the accused at the earliest.”
Article Summary: Bollywood actor Tiger Shroff reportedly took the wheel and rushed his injured driver to hospital. Unidentified assailants opened fire at his car in Mumbai’s Juhu area on Sunday evening. A video of the incident shows the actor switching seats with his driver after the firing.

Article Title: Man stripped, beaten with belts, petrol poured on private parts; video of assault goes viral
Article Text:
(AI image) A disturbing video has surfaced, showing a young man being assaulted in Maharashtra's Latur district.





LATUR: A man was allegedly stripped, beaten with belts, kicked and punched before petrol was poured on his private parts, with the assailants purportedly filming the assault and circulating the video in social media groups. Police in Maharashtra’s Latur district have launched a probe after the footage surfaced, an official said on Sunday.A preliminary inquiry suggests that the incident took place more than two months ago within the jurisdiction of MIDC police station.Police have identified the victim and asked him to come forward to record his statement. He reportedly left the spot after the assault and did not approach the police, the official said.The video purportedly shows the group stripping and assaulting the man before pouring petrol on his private parts.
